observed_mechanics: 0x00841440: MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x8] (8b 54 24 08) loads the second stack word, the Line pointer, into EDX. This is the only memory read performed by the body.
0x00841444: TEST EDX,EDX (85 d2) sets ZF from that word; 0x00841446: JZ 0x00841457 (74 0f) is the function's only conditional branch and the sole difference between its two basic blocks.
0x00841448: LEA EAX,[EDX + -0x4] (8d 42 fc) forms the back-biased pointer. The bias is exactly four bytes, one 32-bit word, and is applied only to the value about to be stored.
0x0084144b: MOV dword ptr [ECX + 0x30],EAX (89 41 30) stores that biased word into receiver offset +0x30. This is the only store performed by the target body itself.

0x0084144e: MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x8],EDX (89 54 24 08) rewrites the second argument slot with the value it already holds, then 0x00841452: JMP 0x0083c780 (e9 29 b3 ff ff) leaves the function. ECX and both stack words are forwarded unchanged.

0x00841457: XOR EAX,EAX (33 c0) / 0x00841459: MOV dword ptr [ECX + 0x30],EAX (89 41 30) is the null arm: it stores a plain zero, not a biased pointer and not the argument. 0x0084145c repeats the value-preserving slot rewrite and 0x00841460: JMP 0x0083c780 (e9 1b b3 ff ff) leaves the same way.

Both arm-rel32 targets resolve to 0x0083c780: 0x00841457 + 0xffffb329 = 0x0083c780 and 0x00841465 + 0xffffb31b = 0x0083c780. The jump displacements are distinct only because the two instructions sit at different addresses.

0x0083c780 is 5 instructions / 15 bytes, raw 8b 44 24 04 8b 54 24 08 89 41 04 89 51 0c c2 08 00: it loads the two stack words into EAX and EDX, writes them to receiver+0x4 and receiver+0xc, and returns with RET 0x8. It writes neither +0x30 nor anything else, so the target's own store survives the tail.
Net effect of 0x00841440 on its receiver is therefore exactly three words: +0x04 = pName, +0x0c = argumentsLine, and +0x30 = argumentsLine ? argumentsLine - 4 : 0.

0x00841440 is a forwarder, not a worker. It contains no loop, no indirect call, no global access, no exception scope record and no SEH frame. All of its non-trivial behaviour is the biased store; the two argument words are consumed by the shared tail.

The sibling thunk at 0x00841410..0x00841430 is instruction-for-instruction the same idiom with a different store offset and a different tail: raw 8b542408 85d2 740f 8d42fc 89410c 89542408 e9c9b3ffff 33c0 89410c 89542408 e9bbb3ff. It stores to receiver+0x0c and tail-jumps to 0x0083c7f0, which is raw 8b442404 894104 c208: the same one-word store to receiver+0x4 with the same RET 0x8. Three further thunks in the same neighbourhood (0x008413e0, 0x008413f0, 0x00841400) instead do ADD ECX,0x4c before jumping, so the family stores into a sub-object at +0x4c in those cases. This establishes the pattern as a linker-emitted wrapper family, not as a one-off body.

0x00841440 is reached from exactly one reference in the whole image, a DATA word at 0x0141c100. There are no direct callers, which is consistent with the briefing's empty callers list and with the function being a virtual-slot target.

The eight dwords 0x0141c0f8..0x0141c11b are 0x008419d0, 0x00841a20, 0x00841440, 0x0083f5d0, 0x0083c7a0, 0x00841a10, 0x0083cc30, 0x0083ca00, and the next word 0x0141c11c is the ASCII text 'Begi'. So the target sits as the third entry of a nine-word code-pointer run interleaved with rodata string literals, not in a contiguous method table.

semantic_findings: Despite the import name CreateDefinitionSafe, the body creates nothing: it performs one conditional biased-pointer store and forwards both arguments to a shared five-instruction setter. There is no allocation, no container insertion, no string handling, no parser lookup and no error reporting anywhere in the 11 instructions.

The two named arguments take opposite roles in the machine. The second one is only null-tested and biased, never read; the first one is not tested at all and is merely forwarded. So the branch that gives the function its two basic blocks is a test of argumentsLine, while the value that decides the returned bool is pName.

The returned bool is a property of pName, not of the store and not of the line. With a non-null pName the call returns true whether or not argumentsLine is null, and with a null pName it returns false even though all three stores still happen. The success flag therefore reports the name, while the biased store reports the line.

The +0x30 word is the function's only original contribution, and it is not a plain assignment: the stored value is the argument minus four bytes whenever the argument is non-null, and zero when it is null. The bias is one-sided and one-shot; nothing in this body ever adds the four back, and no reader of +0x30 is in reach of this package.

The value-preserving rewrite of [ESP+0x8] on both arms is dead in effect. EDX is loaded from that slot at 0x00841440 and is not modified before either store to it, so both writes reproduce the value already present. Whatever motivated the compiler to emit it, it cannot be observed by any caller.

0x00841440 is one member of a family of near-identical forwarders rather than a unique body. 0x00841410 repeats the idiom byte for byte against receiver+0x0c and a one-store tail, and three neighbours at 0x008413e0/0x008413f0/0x00841400 apply ADD ECX,0x4c first, so the same shape is retargeted at different sub-objects. This is the signature of linker-folded or outlined wrapper thunks, and it means the surrounding region should be reconstructed as a family, not function by function.

The tail 0x0083c780 is shared far beyond this class: 29 direct call sites and one data word elsewhere in the image enter it. It is a generic two-word setter (receiver+0x4 and receiver+0xc from the two stack arguments, RET 0x8) with no class identity of its own, so attributing it to FormatParser would be an invention. It is therefore modelled as an unresolved dependency port rather than promoted to a function record.

Both stores the tail performs land on words this function's own logic never consults, and the tail never touches +0x30. The split is clean: the target owns one word, the shared helper owns two, and neither disturbs the other.
Nothing in this body resolves the receiver's concrete class. There is no indirect call and no vtable read, so even if a vtable were pinned down, this function would not consume it.

The naming discrepancy between the SDK prototype and the exported decompilation is a real, unresolved conflict rather than a settled point: the SDK says the second parameter is argumentsLine, the decompiler labels the tested slot pName, and the unsafe sibling supports the SDK ordering. The record adopts the sibling-based ordering and says so.

unresolved_questions: What is the word at receiver displacement 0x30? The body writes it on every call and reads it on none, biasing the second stack word down by one dword. Nothing read for this target names the member or says what an address one dword below the second argument denotes. The arithmetic is modelled; the meaning is not asserted, and the model deliberately gives the word no member name.

Why is the line pointer biased by four bytes before being stored at +0x30, and who reads that word back? The idiom recurs in the adjacent thunk at 0x00841410 against +0x0c, whose two jumps decode to 0x0083c7f0, so it is a family-wide shape rather than an artefact of this body. Its meaning is not recoverable from this VA alone.

What is the true FormatParser layout, and how wide is the receiver? This package models 0x34 bytes, the minimum covering every displacement this call writes, and claims nothing beyond. The SDK structure places +0x30 inside a 0x20-byte mParsers at +0x2c, which contradicts a single biased-pointer store performed on every call, so at least one of the two is wrong.

Which parameter name belongs to the tested slot? The machine fixes that the body tests the second ordinary stack word, entry [ESP+0x8]. The persisted record calls entry [ESP+0x4] pName and entry [ESP+0x8] argumentsLine on the SDK prototype and the unsafe sibling 0x00844fb0; the exported decompilation labels the tested slot pName, which follows from that export placing the receiver at [ESP+0x4] and is refuted by the tail's RET 0x8. This package follows the persisted record. The model test asserts against the second stack word directly, so resolving the naming question cannot change any modelled effect. Settling it needs a caller or a native rebuild.

Is the returned bool a deliberate success flag on the first word, or does the first word simply leak through EAX because the tail had no other choice? EAX is never written by this body; the observed value is whatever 0x0083c780 leaves there, which its first instruction MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4] loaded from the first stack argument. Nothing in the static evidence distinguishes the two, and no caller of this function has been found to read the result. The model implements the observed behaviour and adds no meaning to it.

Why does the derived ABI record abstain (ABI_UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN) when the body plainly tail-jumps a single target from both arms? tools/reconstruction_tooling/abi_infer.py gates tail forwarding on len(state.jmps_direct) == 1 and this body has two direct jumps (0x00841452 and 0x00841460), so the forward is never attempted and the convention is left unnamed. This is a property of the machine evidence and of the inference engine, not of the reconstruction, and it is the sole remaining WARN on the static dimension.

Is 0x0141c100 a genuine second reference to this function, and is the briefing's vtable:0x0141c0f4 real? read_memory 0x0141c0e0 shows 0x0141c0f4 holding 62 6c 65 00, the NUL of the string "Sets a vector4 variable", so the vtable claim is a false positive. What reads the code-pointer run beginning at 0x0141c0f8, of which this function is the third entry, is unresolved, and that bears directly on whether the function is dispatched virtually at all.

Were the three conflict-ledger entries anchored on this VA ever adjudicated? All three record the resolution 'the available observation is retained without semantic promotion', with the reason 'Runtime reachability is absent or the required direct body/call path is not recovered'. This package supplies the static mechanics and does not supply the missing reachability, so those entries stand unchanged.
